module_title: Energy Resources in India - Basic Classification and Coal
introduction: Energy resources are the fundamental driving force behind a nation's modernization, industrialization, and daily transportation. In geography, these resources are broadly classified into two categories: Conventional (traditional, exhaustible, and polluting sources like coal, petroleum, and natural gas) and Non-Conventional (renewable, sustainable sources like solar, wind, and tidal energy). At this beginner level, we will focus on understanding the foundational conventional fossil fuels that currently power the vast majority of India's economy.

core_concepts.title: Coal: The Backbone of Indian Industry
core_concepts.description: Coal is the most abundantly available fossil fuel in India and acts as the prime source of energy for electricity generation (thermal power) and heavy industries like iron and steel smelting. It is a combustible black sedimentary rock formed from the remains of ancient forests over millions of years. India is highly dependent on coal, making it one of the top producers and consumers of this mineral globally.

core_concepts.title: The Four Grades of Coal
core_concepts.description: Depending on the degree of compression, depth, and time of burial, coal is classified into four ranks based on carbon content. 1. Peat: The first stage of formation with low carbon and high moisture. 2. Lignite: A low-grade brown coal, soft with high moisture. 3. Bituminous: The most widely used commercial coal, buried deep and subjected to high temperatures. 4. Anthracite: The highest quality hard coal, containing over 80% carbon, producing the most heat and least smoke.

core_concepts.title: Petroleum (Liquid Gold)
core_concepts.description: Petroleum, or crude oil, is the next major energy source in India after coal. It provides fuel for heat and lighting, lubricants for machinery, and raw materials for a number of manufacturing industries, including synthetic textiles, fertilizers, and numerous chemical industries. Because of its immense economic value and wide range of by-products, petroleum is often referred to as 'Liquid Gold'.

core_concepts.title: Natural Gas: The Cleaner Alternative
core_concepts.description: Natural gas is an important clean energy resource found either in association with petroleum or independently in separate gas reservoirs. It is considered an environment-friendly fuel because it produces significantly lower carbon dioxide emissions compared to coal and petroleum. It is heavily used as a raw material in the petrochemical industry and as Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) for vehicles.

important_entities.name: Gondwana Coal
important_entities.key_fact: Accounts for 98% of India's Coal Reserves
important_entities.significance: Indian coal is geologically divided into two main rock series: Gondwana and Tertiary. Gondwana coal is over 200 million years old, highly metallurgical (Bituminous), and is massive in quantity, making up 98% of India's total coal reserves. It is primarily located in the Damodar Valley across Jharkhand and West Bengal.

important_entities.name: Digboi
important_entities.key_fact: The Oldest Oil Well in India
important_entities.significance: Located in the state of Assam, Digboi is a historic site. It is not only the oldest operational oil well in India but also the place where crude oil was discovered for the very first time in the country during the late 19th century by the British.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume that because India has massive coal reserves, it has plenty of high-quality coal. This is a major misconception. India has very limited reserves of the highest-grade 'Anthracite' coal. It is found almost exclusively in the Kalakot region of Jammu and Kashmir. Most of India's coal is of the 'Bituminous' grade.

Do not confuse Coal with Charcoal. Coal is a naturally occurring fossil fuel extracted from the earth through mining. Charcoal is an artificial, man-made product created by burning wood in a low-oxygen environment.

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: Order of Coal Quality (Best to Worst)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use this acronym to remember the decreasing order of carbon content and quality: Anthracite (Best) -> Bituminous -> Lignite -> Peat (Worst).

exam_strategy_tips: In exams, if asked about the primary source of commercial energy in India, always select 'Coal'. It still accounts for over half of the country's commercial energy requirements.
Remember that petroleum is always found in the pores of 'Sedimentary' rocks, never in igneous or metamorphic rocks.
